known_facts_book1: The girl Ruler of the whole Land of Oz, dignified on her emerald throne and a joyous ordinary girl in her private apartments.
Was stolen as a baby by the Witch Mombi and transformed into a boy, and was restored to her proper person by Glinda; she tells this story herself at dinner.
Made the Law forbidding anyone but Glinda the Good and her assistant the Wizard to practice magic, because the Witches and Magicians used their powers for evil.
Made a second Law forbidding anyone to pick a six-leaved clover or gather the herbs Witches boil, because those were used in unlawful charms.
Owns a Magic Picture in her room that shows any scene in the Land of Oz where strangers or travelers happen to be.
Orders the arrest of Ojo the Unlucky before he reaches the city gate, having seen the offense.
Forgives Ojo at his trial, saying he is penitent and has been punished enough, and lets him keep the picked clover.
Has Dr. Pipt brought to the palace, his four kettles destroyed and his book of recipes burned, and has the two marble statues brought there too.
Is guarded in the Throne Room by the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger, who crouch at her feet.
Gives Ojo and Unc Nunkie a house just outside the walls of the Emerald City and takes them under her protection.
Decrees that Scraps shall be preserved as one of the curiosities of Oz, free to live where she pleases.

known_facts_book1: Once a girl of the Kansas prairies, now a Princess of Oz living in the royal palace as Ozma's best friend, and still a simple little girl in a plain white frock.
Her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em, her only relatives, have also been brought to Oz by Ozma and given a pleasant home.
Discovered the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Cowardly Lion and Tik-tok the Clockwork Man on her earlier journeys.
Asks Ozma's leave to go with Ojo because she knows Oz and he does not, and brings a gold flask holding a pint for the dark-well water.
Travels in a plain gingham dress and a checked sunbonnet as best fitted for travel.
Slaps and pushes the Tottenhots to rescue the Scarecrow and the Patchwork Girl from being tossed about, and bargains with them for a night's shelter.
Sews up the hole in the Scarecrow's back and the rip in his leg after the picket fence.
Explains the Horners' joke to the Hoppers by telling them to laugh at it, and so ends the war.
Calms the Quadling's angry wife by promising to send them goods from the Emerald City, including a new clothesline.

known_facts_book1: A little old man, once a humbug who knew no magic at all, now reformed and taking lessons from Glinda the Good as her humble Assistant.
Is with Glinda the only person licensed by Ozma's Law to practice magic in the Land of Oz.
Exposes Scraps's trick at Ojo's trial, making the clover sprout from the golden vase into a bush before the whole court.
By royal edict deprives Dr. Pipt of all power to work magic, and with the same gesture straightens every crooked limb of the man's body.
Removes the Glass Cat's pink brains and replaces them with transparent ones, curing her conceit.
Sends the Woozy to the Royal Menagerie and announces Ozma's decisions for Scraps and for Ojo.
Restores Margolotte and then Unc Nunkie to life with a magic pass and a magic word, using a method Glinda taught him — not Dr. Pipt's recipe.

known_facts_book1: The great Sorceress of Oz, the Royal Sorceress and the only one besides her assistant the Wizard permitted to practice magic.
Owns a big book in which every event that takes place anywhere in the world is recorded the moment it happens.
Taught the reformed Wizard his magic, so that he is no longer a humbug.
Restored Ozma to her proper person when Ozma arrived at the Emerald City as Tip.
Knew all about Dr. Pipt's magic-making, the accident, and Ojo's quest, and knew in advance that Ojo would fail to find all five things.
Sent for the Wizard and instructed him in the one other way to destroy the charm of the Liquid of Petrifaction.
Does not appear in person anywhere in this book; she acts only through the Wizard and is spoken of by others.
